title: Eight Views of Autumn Moods
medium: album of eight leaves, on paper

source.label: Sirén: pictures of 1623–24 show “Tung's manner at the time of his richest production”
Waley: Dong “completely identifies the Learned Man's Painting with the Southern School”
Wikipedia: “Eight Views of Autumn Moods, dated 1620. Album of eight leaves”

work.text: For [this] purpose sketchy records on album-leaves or other paintings of small size were quite satisfactory, and consequently it is not surprising to find that a large portion of Tung Ch'i-ch'ang's painted work [consists] of such minor pictures, executed mainly in ink, [sometimes] with the addition of light colours.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (The Later Ming and Leading Ch‘ing Masters)

moment.text: His work favored expression over formal likeness. He also avoided anything he deemed to be slick or sentimental. This led him to create landscapes with intentionally distorted spatial features.

matters.text: Whatever he wrote or painted reflected [the] rhythm of his own [mind] and hand, and he was a true master of [the] brush.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V (The Later Ming and Leading Ch‘ing Masters)
